claims.text: Yes, there is a cap. i-on's liability to the Customer is limited to one month's fees plus the remaining portion of any prepaid fees, for any cause, whether in contract or in tort.

citations.quote: i-on's liability for damages to the Customer for any cause whatsoever, regardless of the form of action, and whether in contract or in tort, including negligence, shall be limited to one (1) month's fees and the remaining portion of any prepaid fees.

claims.text: Separately from the cap, i-on will not be liable for lost profits or other consequential damages, even if it was advised such damages were possible.

citations.quote: i-on will not be liable under any circumstances for any lost profits or other consequential damages, even if i-on has been advised as to the possibility of such damages.

claims.text: The sources do not list any carve-outs or exceptions from the liability cap (for example, for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or indemnification obligations). The cap is stated to apply to damages for any cause whatsoever.

citations.quote: for any cause whatsoever, regardless of the form of action

claims.text: The Customer also gives related hold-harmless protections for service interruptions and data loss, which are not framed as exclusions from the cap.

citations.quote: agrees to hold i-on harmless for any interruptions in service to the Hosted Site
agrees to hold i-on harmless for any such data loss for the Hosted Site, provided that i-on maintains reasonable steps as described in this Agreement to protect against such data loss.
